title: get
description: A traversal-first helper for the terminal: `get` makes the cd+ls workflow fast for folders, and additionally provides support for viewing files in bat, cat, vim, and supports reading links/PATH items.

content.heading: get - fast cd+ls workflow for folders, with file viewing and search
content: `get` is a traversal-first helper for the terminal: most invocations are a single `get` away from where you are, and the `-` back-navigation keeps a history of the directories you've been in. The purpose of `get` is to make the cd+ls workflow fast for folders — and it additionally provides support for viewing files in bat, cat, and vim, and supports reading links/PATH items.

`get` is implemented as a bash function (for cd support), backed by `got` — the POSIX-sh script holding all the logic (listing, cat/bat display, grep, filename search + fzf picking, `$PATH` resolution).

content.heading: Usage
content: get @name [more...]              open <name> in $EDITOR; if not a local file, resolve it on $PATH and follow symlinks to the real file
get <dir> [names...]             ls the dir, then find each name beneath it
get <file...>                    cat/bat the files; symlinks print only their real path, so `get $(get <link>)` shows the contents
get <queries...> <file|dir>      grep each query (with file+line numbers); for a folder, find matching filenames and fzf-pick one
get <queries...> -- <file|dir>…  same, with an explicit queries/targets split
get -                            cd to the previous directory first
get <dir> [names...]             cd into <dir>, then behave like `got .`

content.heading: Split rule
content: Without `--`: an argument that exists as a file/dir is a target, everything else is a query. If there are no queries at all, targets are displayed; if there are queries, targets are searched.

content.heading: Implementation
content: `get` is implemented as a bash function (for cd support), backed by `got` — the POSIX-sh script holding all the logic (listing, cat/bat display, grep, filename search + fzf picking, `$PATH` resolution).
